items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: When we had the Trump election, nobody had Trump signs in our neighborhood.

ctx.x: Maybe it’s the news that I choose to watch and the polls, but it seems like the majority of the country now feels like that. And it’s a minority that’s keeping the country down and with terrible intentions.

Yeah I mean I think it depends on, that’s why social media does us no good. Because if we just have our circle of friends we only see what they post. If you just watch CNN you only see what they say about these issues. When we had the Trump election, nobody had Trump signs in our neighborhood. All those people voted for Trump. And I don’t know who they’re going to vote for this time. But all my friends voted for Trump. And that’s what they did and I have some nice neighbors. I love my neighbors. I have a few that…

I appreciate your eloquent opinions. Just to wrap up, were you in the position, when all the cancellations of gigs started coming in, usually you were told, okay the gig is off, the thing is cancelled. Did you have to cancel anything yourself, out of feeling for your own protection or the thinking of your sidemen or whatever else?
